Finland.text: The 2026 report made it the happiest country for the ninth year in a row.
Finland.evidence: As of March 2026, Finland has been ranked the happiest country in the world for nine years in a row.

Iceland.text: It had essentially no mosquitoes until October 2025.
Iceland.evidence: Iceland was essentially free of mosquitoes until October 2025.

Denmark.text: Its royal line goes back to Gorm the Old, king in the early 900s.
Denmark.evidence: The extant Danish monarchy traces its roots back to Gorm the Old, who established his reign in the early 10th century.

Costa Rica.text: It abolished its army in 1948; the money now goes to health care and schools.
Costa Rica.evidence: On 1 December 1948, Costa Rica abolished its military force. ... The budget previously dedicated to the military is now dedicated to providing health care services and education.

Sweden.evidence: The 1814 campaign was the last time Sweden was at war.

Norway.text: Every December it gives Britain a Christmas tree, as thanks for British help in the Second World War.
Norway.evidence: Every December Norway gives a Christmas tree to the United Kingdom as thanks for the British assistance during the war.

Netherlands.text: A quarter of all trips there are made by bicycle.
Netherlands.evidence: Around half of all trips are made by car, 25% by bicycle, 20% walking, and 5% by public transport.

Israel.text: In the report's top 10 every year since 2022: #9, then #4, #5, #8 and #8 again this year.
Israel.evidence: The page's ranking tables: 2022 report, 9 Israel; 2023 report, 4 Israel; 2024 report, 5 Israel 7.341; 2025 report, 8 Israel 7.234; 2026 report, 8 Israel 7.187. 2020 report, 14 Israel.

Luxembourg.text: In 2020 it became the first country to make all public transport free.
Luxembourg.evidence: In 2020, Luxembourg became the first country in the world to provide free public transport at a national scale.

Switzerland.text: Its citizens can force a national vote on any law parliament passes.
Switzerland.evidence: Through optional referendums, citizens may challenge any law passed by parliament.
